rules.label: Income at or below 250% FPL qualifies for discounted care
rules.quote: If your gross household income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty level: You may be able to get discounts on your health services.

notes: Policy is a patient-facing summary of Colorado Hospital Discounted Care law (effective September 1, 2022).
Residency (Colorado) and service-area requirements are implied by state law but not explicit in this text.
Insurance status does not bar eligibility: uninsured patients must be screened for public programs; insured patients have the right to request screening.
Hospital must check eligibility within 45 days of service or request to be screened.
Decision notification within 14 days of completing an application.
Appeal window: 30 days from date hospital gave the decision.

Before sending to collections, hospital must: screen for eligibility, offer payment plan if eligible, explain bill in primary language, bill insurance if applicable, notify patient of potential collections.
Provider (physician) monthly bill capped at 2% of monthly income (not modeled in payment_plan).
Maximum bill rates for services are set by the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing.
Immigration status and citizenship do not affect eligibility.
Patient may refuse screening but may lose right to legal action for failure to screen or discount.
Complaints can be filed with hospital, provider, or Department of Health Care Policy and Financing.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Proved: every Colorado resident at or below 250% of the poverty line qualifies for help under this policy's written rules.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts

findings.title: Ignores assets for Colorado-protected households

law.quote: THE METHODOLOGY MUST NOT CONSIDER A PATIENT'S ASSETS.
